newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed sharply lower on Tuesday, due to active selling from local investors who were discouraged by the Chicago market's price falls overnight and the stronger yen, traders said.
Prices were 200 to 420 yen lower, with the benchmark July 1998 contract down 290 yen at 14,400 yen per tonne. The day's estimated trade volume was 35,614 lots.
Active selling capped the topside from the opening, traders said. "We had two bearish factors, the weaker Chicago market and the strong yen," a brokerage house trader said.
The soybean market's sharp price losses also accelerated the selling orders, traders said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.68-1/4 per bushel at 0810 GMT, against $2.68-1/2 at Monday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.38-1/4 a bushel at 0810 GMT, against $8.38-1/2 at Monday's close.
